q: A Bill has lain with a Governor for two years without action. Which settled proposition applies?
options: A court may direct decision within reasonable time; settled law grants no deemed assent
A court may deem assent after three months
No remedy exists against gubernatorial inaction
The Governor must assent as directed
expl: Direction-to-decide remedy is settled; deemed assent has no settled-law status and is under reference.
why: Prolonged inaction is justiciable for a decision-direction. Assent itself cannot be directed, nor assent deemed.
trapnote: Direction to decide is not direction to assent.

q: An officer states that a Governor may pardon any offence committed within the State. Which statement is correct?
options: The statement is accurate: a Governor's power extends to every offence in the State
The statement is too narrow: a Governor may also pardon offences under Union laws
The statement is too wide: a Governor may only remit and never commute a sentence
The statement is too wide: court martial sentences and death-sentence pardons are outside
expl: Two carve-outs apply: court martial sentences and the pardon of a death sentence.
why: The fourth option identifies the statement as too wide but misdescribes the carve-out, a right diagnosis with a wrong reason.
trapnote: Two carve-outs, both about scope. Remission and commutation are available to a Governor.

q: The 2023 reservation amendment is cited to claim that a Council of Ministers must now include one-third women. Which statement is correct?
options: The citation succeeds: the amendment extends to the composition of Councils
The citation fails: the amendment applies only after the Council is reconstituted
The citation fails: the amendment concerns seats in legislatures, not ministerial office
The citation succeeds subject to the fifteen per cent ceiling on Council size
expl: The amendment reserves seats in directly elected Houses; it says nothing about ministerial office.
why: The fourth option combines two real rules to produce a proposition neither of them supports.
trapnote: Combining two real rules does not create a third. Check what each actually governs.

q: Consider ordinances during a period of President's Rule in a State: 1-The President may promulgate ordinances for the State. 2-The Governor continues to promulgate them. 3-The six-week rule ceases to apply. Which is/are correct?
options: 2 and 3 only
1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
None of them
expl: Only Presidential ordinances for the State hold; Governor role displaced, six-week expiry continues.
why: Where the State legislature stands dissolved or suspended, the legislative function passes to Parliament and the President.
trapnote: President's Rule transfers the legislative function. The expiry rules continue to operate.

q: A claim is made that the criminal statutes in force from July 2024 removed the requirement of a Governor's sanction in specified prosecutions. Which statement is correct?
options: The claim fails: sanction requirements arise under separate provisions and continue
The claim succeeds: the new statutes dispensed with all sanction requirements
The claim fails: sanction was never required in any prosecution at any time
The claim succeeds where the accused holds an office of profit under the State
expl: Sanction requirements arise under other provisions and were not swept away by the new statutes.
why: The third option reaches the right conclusion by denying that sanction ever existed, which is itself wrong.
trapnote: A right conclusion drawn from a false premise remains a wrong option.

q: Following the creation of twenty-six districts in Andhra Pradesh, a claim is made that the Council of Ministers may be enlarged proportionately. Which statement is correct?
options: The claim succeeds: the ceiling is computed on the number of administrative districts
The claim fails: the ceiling applies only to the Union Council of Ministers
The claim succeeds where the Assembly has approved the reorganisation
The claim fails: the ceiling is fixed by reference to the strength of the Assembly
expl: The ceiling is fifteen per cent of the Assembly's strength, which reorganisation does not alter.
why: The third option denies that the ceiling applies to States at all, which is a distinct and separate error.
trapnote: The ceiling is computed on House strength, which district reorganisation does not change.

q: The 2024 ruling on community resources is cited to justify an ordinance acquiring private land without legislative consideration. Which statement is correct?
options: The citation succeeds: the ruling permits acquisition by ordinance in the public interest
The citation fails on one count: the ruling widened the directive but laying is mandatory
The citation fails on two counts: the ruling narrowed the directive and ordinances must be laid
The citation fails on one count: the ruling narrowed the directive but laying is optional
expl: The ruling narrowed the directive, and the obligation to lay an ordinance is mandatory.
why: Two options identify a single defect, so a candidate stopping at the first error selects a near miss.
trapnote: Where a proposition fails on two independent grounds, the complete option names both.

q: Consider the November 2022 ruling in relation to the executive: 1-It concerned reservation. 2-It altered the veto powers of the President. 3-It left the pardoning power untouched. Which is/are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
expl: The ruling concerned reservation and did not touch the veto or the pardoning power.
why: The third statement is true but incidental, testing whether a candidate rejects true statements that seem beside the point.
trapnote: A statement can be both accurate and incidental. Incidental is not the same as false.

q: An ordinance is promulgated one week before the legislature reassembles and is never placed before it. Which statement is correct?
options: It expires six weeks after reassembly, and the omission to lay it is an abuse
It expires one week after reassembly, the period running from promulgation
It continues in force, the obligation to lay it being directory in nature
It expires immediately on reassembly, the House not having been informed
expl: The six-week clock runs from reassembly, and the obligation to lay it is mandatory.
why: The second option runs the clock from the wrong event, and the third demotes a mandatory duty.
trapnote: Two separate rules: when the ordinance expires, and the duty to place it before the House.

q: A Governor recalls that a Bill may be reserved and asks whether reservation is available at every stage. Which statement is correct?
options: Reservation is available at any stage, including after the Bill has received assent
Reservation is available only where the State Council of Ministers so advises
Reservation is available only where the Bill has been returned and re-passed once
Reservation is available when the Bill is first presented, and is obligatory in one category
expl: Reservation operates at presentation and is compulsory where a Bill would derogate from High Court powers.
why: The second option extends the power beyond assent, which would make assent revocable and is plainly wrong.
trapnote: Reservation operates before assent. Once assent is given the Bill is beyond recall.
